item.title: Commutative rings with square-difference factor absorbing factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.20884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study sdf-absorbing factorization rings (SAF-rings), in which every regular ideal is a finite product of square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We investigate their behavior under direct products, localizations, factor rings, and module idealizations, and establish connections with SP-rings, Dedekind rings, and N-rings. We also introduce strongly sdf-absorbing factorization rings (SSAF-rings), relate them to SSP-rings and almost multiplication rings, and prove that the Noetherian SSAF-rings are precisely the ZPI-rings. Applications to module idealizations and monoid rings are also presented.
item.dc:creator: Malik Tusif Ahmed, Hafnaoui Hidouri, Ahmed Hamed

item.title: Holomorphy rings and the Nullstellensatz over large fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.21039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an infinite field $K$ and an ideal $I\subseteq K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, let $J(Z_K(I))$ be the ideal of polynomials vanishing on the $K$-rational zero locus of $I$. A Nullstellensatz over $K$ is an algebraic description of this closure operator on ideals. Hilbert's classical theorem provides such a description via the radical of $I$ over any algebraically closed field. In the present article, we introduce a unifying framework for Nullstellens\"atze over arbitrary rings using the notion of an $A$-radical, for $A$ is a subring of $K(X)$ containing $K[X]$. We show that a single canonical holomorphy ring gives a Nullstellensatz over every infinite field, recovering Hilbert's theorem when $K$ is algebraically closed. In addition, we give a new characterization of large fields (in the sense of Pop) via a particular Nullstellensatz: a perfect field is large exactly when the \emph{rational} holomorphy ring $A_n(K)$--the intersection of all $K$-rational places of residue field exactly $K$--satisfies the corresponding Nullstellensatz. Finally we study the order structure of the class of rings $A$ for which the $A$-radical gives a Nullstellensatz. We show that over non-algebraically closed fields this class has no minimal element, showing there is no optimal Nullstellensatz over such fields.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Sebasti\'an Uribe Rinc\'on

item.title: On the variety of sum of powers of certain complete intersection forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.21544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a homogeneous polynomial (form). If the annihilator ideal $F^\perp$ is a complete intersection, then $F$ is called as a complete intersection form. For many complete intersection forms, we show that its minimal apolar ideal is a complete intersection and further we show that ${\rm VSP}(F)$ is irreducible and compute its dimension.
item.dc:creator: Meghana Bhat, Ronnie Sebastian

item.title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.
item.dc:creator: Nursel Erey, T\`ai Huy H\`a, Takayuki Hibi, Selvi Kara, Susan Morey

item.title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.
item.dc:creator: Guocheng Dai, Jiangsheng Hu

item.title: The asymptotic surjective number and F-surjective signature
item.description: arXiv:2610.22104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two invariants measuring the asymptotic abundance of surjections between modules. We prove that Hashimoto's asymptotic surjective number is attained over local rings, hence it is a rational number. We also prove that its associated function is constructible in families and on spectra; on the latter, it is moreover lower semicontinuous on the support of the target. We establish the existence of the F-surjective signature, a common generalization of F-signature and dual F-signature, and prove that it is superadditive in its source and varies lower semicontinuously across the spectrum under mild assumptions. As applications, we obtain new rationality results for dual F-signature and prove a transformation inequality under finite maps, with consequences for quotient singularities and reduction mod p.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Smirnov, Kevin Tucker

item.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.20649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that matroid Stanley-Reisner rings can have essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, even at corank three. For every $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid with $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order deformation classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. These classes define a joint flat family whose $(m-1)$-jet has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, every nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and this quotient has an explicit module presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators. The construction is based on a computation of the full multigraded second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and its primary cup image in terms of flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. This computation also proves that $T^2$ vanishes precisely when every connected component has corank at most two, equivalently when the matroid has no $U_{1,4}$-minor, settling the conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello. The same criterion characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang

item.title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.
item.dc:creator: Yohji Akama

item.title: Perfectoid Pure and Signature Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend perfectoid purity and related invariants to divisor pairs in mixed characteristic. The resulting purity condition agrees with $F$-purity of pairs in characteristic $p$ as defined by Hara--Watanabe. For normal (respectively, demi-normal) log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs, we show that perfectoid pure implies log canonical (respectively, semi-log canonical). We similarly establish adjunction for perfectoid pure pairs and inversion of adjunction for principal pairs in complete intersections along a Cartier divisor. We also define perfectoid pure thresholds and prove localization and base change results, including a formula for local extensions with regular closed fiber. We establish upper bounds in terms of analytic spread, dimension, and log canonical thresholds. Finally, we also introduce perfectoid signatures for divisor pairs in mixed characteristic whose positivity characterizes the BCM-regularity of log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs. We prove a transformation rule under finite extensions and show continuity and convexity for scalings of a Cartier divisor.
item.dc:creator: Hanlin Cai, Anne Fayolle, Linquan Ma, Karl Schwede, Ilya Smirnov, Kevin Tucker, Joe Waldron

item.title: Gluing weak approximability along recollements
item.description: arXiv:2610.22161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study whether weak approximability glues along recollements of triangulated categories that are compactly generated by a single object. This is applied to derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and prescribed support for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pat Lank

item.title: Deterministic Determination of Axial Constants, Sectional Regularities and Annihilator Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Axial constants and sectional regularities are recently introduced invariants of homogeneous polynomial ideals that, like the already earlier introduced annihilator numbers, depend on generic choices of coordinates. We provide effective characterisations of the genericity underlying these invariants in terms of $\beta$-maximal position and strong stability. In particular, we show that $\beta$-maximal position suffices for determining generic annihilator numbers and sectional regularities, while its combination with strong stability yields corresponding results for axial constants. We also develop deterministic linear algebra procedures for detecting the required generic positions and for computing these invariants.
item.dc:creator: Amir Hashemi, Rozhin Sadr, Werner M. Seiler

item.title: Homological Detection by Perfectoid Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.17801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We first establish estimates for the projective and injective dimensions for quotients of perfectoid algebras by radical ideals. As applications, we obtain homological characterizations of modules of finite injective dimension, (big) Cohen--Macaulay modules, Gorenstein local rings, and regular local rings in mixed characteristic in terms of perfectoid algebras. These are mixed characteristic analogues of the corresponding characterizations via Frobenius morphisms in positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Ryo Ishizuka

item.title: Truncations of the ring of number-theoretic functions, revisited
item.description: arXiv:2608.29555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a field containing $\mathbb{Q}$, let $\Gamma$ be the ring of all functions from the positive integers to $K$ under Dirichlet convolution, and let $\Gamma_n$ be its truncation to functions supported on $[1,n]$. In [Snellman, Homology Homotopy Appl. 2 (2000), 17-27; arXiv:math/9904143] it was shown that $\Gamma_n$ is a polynomial ring modulo a monomial ideal $I_n$ which is stable after reversing the order of the variables, and the Poincare-Betti series of $\Gamma_n$ was computed in terms of the numbers $C_{n,v}$ of minimal generators of $I_n$ of least support $v$. We prove that $C_{n,v} = \Phi(n,p_v)$, Legendre's sifting function: the number of integers in $[1,n]$ free of prime factors $\le p_v$. This identifies an invariant of a minimal free resolution with a classical object of sieve theory, and it refines to the grading by total degree, with the number of prime factors carried in a variable. As consequences we obtain: a proof of Conjecture 4.6 of the 2000 paper, which was left open there; the asymptotics $C_n \sim \pi(n)^2/2$ of the total number of minimal generators, showing that the lower bound $C_n \ge \binom{\pi(n)+1}{2}$ of that paper is asymptotically sharp, together with the exact order $C_n - \binom{\pi(n)+1}{2} \sim \frac{16}{3} n^{3/2} / \log^3 n$ of the error; and the identification of $C_n$ with the OEIS sequence A182843. We also record errata for the 2000 paper: one stated result is false, one worked example is miscomputed, and two proofs are incomplete. Corrected statements and complete proofs are given.
item.dc:creator: Jan Snellman

item.title: Quasi-projective dimensions of complexes over rings
item.description: arXiv:2604.09279v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quasi-projective dimension of modules over associative rings is generalized in this paper to the one of complexes of modules. Basic properties of this dimension are established, including a comparison result with projective dimension and a derived Auslander-Buchsbaum formula for complexes of finite quasi-projective dimension. Several sufficient conditions are provided for a commutative noetherian local ring to be a complete intersection under the assumption that each finitely generated module has finite quasi-projective dimension. This provides some positive answers to an open question on quasi-projective dimension proposed by Gheibi-Jorgensen-Takahashi. Moreover, the behavior of quasi-projective dimension under taking the quotient of a commutative ring modulo a regular sequence is investigated, and some partial results toward the change-of-rings question on quasi-projective dimension are given.
item.dc:creator: Hongxing Chen, Jiangsheng Hu, Xiaoyan Yang

item.title: Adjoint test modules along Cohen--Macaulay morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2605.07956v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a transformation rule for adjoint test modules along Cohen--Macaulay maps between Cohen--Macaulay varieties that have $F$-rational geometric fibers. This is, in part, an effective version of Enescu's theorem on the ascent of $F$-rationality under local maps with $F$-rational geometric fibers.
item.dc:creator: Javier Carvajal-Rojas, Axel St\"abler

item.title: Local stability of Frobenius and Artin--Schreier base-change: a comparison
item.description: arXiv:2608.24256v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(X,\Delta)\to C$ be a family of pairs over a smooth curve in positive characteristic $p>0$. We study the discrepancies of divisors over the base-change $(X,\Delta)\to C$ along Artin--Schreier and Frobenius covers of $C$, through ramification data for Artin--Schreier and degree $p$ purely inseparable extensions of DVRs. As an application, we recover a result of Hu and Zong about permanence of local stability for such base-change.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Posva

item.title: The ozone group of $U_q^+(B_2)$
item.description: arXiv:2609.04919v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the ozone group of \(U_q^{+}(B_2)\). More precisely, if \(\ell=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)\) when \(q\) is a root of unity, we obtain $$ \operatorname{Oz}(U_q^{+}(B_2)) \cong \begin{cases} \mu_2 , & \text{if \(q\) is not a root of unity},\\[2mm] \mu_{\gcd(\ell,2)}, & \text{if \(q\) is a primitive \(m\)-th root of unity, \(m\geq5\).} \end{cases} $$ We also study several homological properties of \(U_q^{+}(B_2)\), showing that it is Artin--Schelter regular of global dimension \(4\), Auslander-regular, Cohen--Macaulay, strongly Noetherian, and skew Calabi--Yau. Using two different iterated Ore presentations, we show that its Nakayama automorphism is trivial for every $q \in \K^*$, so $U_q^{+}(B_2)$ is Calabi--Yau of dimension $4$; for $q$ not a root of unity this also follows from work of Goodearl and Yakimov. When $q$ is a primitive $m$-th root of unity with $m\geq5$, we deduce that the center is Gorenstein, we check directly that the ozone group acts with trivial homological determinant, and we describe the nonzero normal elements in terms of the ozone group.
item.dc:creator: James G\'omez, Helbert Venegas

item.title: The $\lambda$-chain condition for unit interval determinantal fiber rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.15971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is shown that certain finite partially ordered sets arising from unit interval determinantal facet ideals satisfy the $\lambda$-chain condition. In addition, their applications to commutative algebra are briefly discussed.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Sora Miyashita
